subject: Request: SLA carveout for preview model rollout
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@olivesolutions.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@olivesolutions.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preview model — SLA expectations and exception request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited about the preview of the new condensed-m7 model for document understanding — it materially improves latency on our ingestion pipeline. Before we move to a week-long public demo for internal stakeholders, procurement and security need written guidance on any SLA differences for preview / beta models.

Specifically they asked:
- Will Redwood commit to the same uptime SLA for preview models as for GA models?
- If not, can we get an exception / carveout that documents expected availability and an agreed escalation path so our demo team can prepare?
- Any maximum latency SLOs you can commit to during the demo window?

I’ve attached the release notes you shared with product, and procurement included a short form they’d like completed (procurement-sla-exception-form.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a written exception or whether preview models are strictly excluded from SLA coverage?

If possible we need something in writing by end of day Wednesday (10 Mar) to keep the demo schedule. Appreciate a direct call if easier.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Olive Solutions
samira.k@olivesolutions.com
+1 415 555 0189

Attachments: preview-model-release-notes.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@olivesolutions.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preview model — SLA expectations and exception request

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear note and for sharing the procurement form. Quick summary up front: we can support a targeted, timeboxed SLA exception for the demo period with specific constraints and mitigations, but preview/preview-label model variants are not covered by our standard GA SLA by default. Below are the practical options we can offer and a proposed next step.

Options we can offer for a demo window (sample approaches):
1) Best-effort with written escalations: Redwood will operate the preview model as best-effort (no uptime SLA), provide a named escalation contact, and commit to 4-hour initial response for Sev 1 incidents during demo hours.
2) Limited availability SLA addendum (timeboxed): For a 7-day demo window we can offer a targeted availability commitment of 99.5% for request routing and allocation, with an explicit exclusion for model training/deployment regressions tied to upstream model changes. This would be captured in a short addendum.
3) Paid guarded capacity: If Olive purchases a small dedicated pool (Reserved/Guarded capacity) for the demo, we can guarantee the standard uptime SLA for that capacity, even if the model is in preview. This is the most reliable route but requires a short commitment and provisioning lead time.

Suggested next steps:
- If procurement needs a written exception, we can prepare a 1‑page SLA exception addendum that clarifies the scope (dates, model id, metrics, escalation contacts).
- We’d like to keep the addendum explicit about known risks: preview model may see behavior changes if upstream model weights are updated, and we’ll exclude roll-forward changes from the availability commitment.
- Laura (legal) and Vivek (ops) are looped to draft minimal language and confirm the escalation contact.

I attached a draft addendum (rwi-sla-exception-addendum.docx) and a short bullet list we can drop into procurement forms. If you can confirm preferred option (1/2/3) and the demo window dates, I’ll get the addendum finalized and send a DocuSign link. Happy to jump on a 20-min call — available 10–12 PT today.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 650 555 0123

Attachments: rwi-sla-exception-addendum.docx
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@olivesolutions.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@olivesolutions.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preview model — SLA expectations and exception request

Karthik,

Thanks — that all helps. Procurement is pushing for an explicit written carveout (option 2) that lists the demo window (15–21 Mar) and a basic uptime target so they can sign off on the demo infrastructure. They also want to see the named escalation contact for Sev 1 and an acknowledgment of the exception in our procurement tracker.

A couple of clarifications they asked me to get from you:
- Can Redwood commit to a maximum average 95th percentile latency of < 400ms for inference requests during demo hours? If not, can we include a best-effort target and an operational plan if we exceed that?
- For the addendum: procurement prefers the language to be a simple single paragraph that we can attach to our POC purchase order.

I’ve filled out the procurement form and attached it here (procurement-sla-exception-form.pdf). If you can send the finalized 1‑page addendum and escalation contact by COB Wednesday (10 Mar), we’ll proceed with the demo schedule.

On the call availability, I can do 11:30 PT today for a quick sync.

—Samira

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preview model — SLA expectations and exception request

Samira / Procurement team —

Appended below is the finalized single‑paragraph addendum we propose for the 15–21 Mar demo window. This is deliberately concise so it can be attached to your POC purchase order. If that looks good I’ll put it in DocuSign and include Vivek as the on-call escalation contact.

---- PROPOSED SLA EXCEPTION ADDENDUM (single paragraph) ----
Redwood Inference agrees to operate the specified preview model (model id: condensed-m7-preview-202603) for the period 2026-03-15 through 2026-03-21 with a targeted availability of 99.5% for request routing and allocation during agreed demo hours (08:00–20:00 PT). This exception is timeboxed to the dates above, excludes outages resulting from upstream model weight changes or scheduled maintenance, and does not constitute an amendment to Redwood’s standard GA SLA. Redwood will provide an initial response to declared Sev 1 incidents within 4 hours during demo hours and will designate an operational escalation contact (Vivek Kulkarni, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com). Any request for an extended or permanent SLA must be handled through Redwood’s standard Dedicated/Reserved capacity process or via a separate commercial agreement.
---- end addendum ----

Latency note: we can include a best‑effort 95th percentile latency target of < 400ms for typical request sizes used in your demo. Given preview label constraints we cannot guarantee a hard latency SLA, but we will instrument detailed latency dashboards for the demo and run a pre-demo smoke test on 2026-03-14 to validate.

Next steps:
- Samira: confirm demo window (15–21 Mar) and that procurement is OK with the single-paragraph wording.
- I’ll create the DocuSign and route to your procurement contact for signature.
- Vivek/ops will run the smoke test on 2026-03-14 and share pre-demo telemetry.

If you’d like any edits to the paragraph, call out the specific language and I’ll update. Thanks for moving quickly on this — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
+1 650 555 0123
